item.title: Newsletter: 🥳 A Win for Transit Access / 🌉 Tonight: SRT Bridge Tour / 🍻 Monday: South Street Meetup
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #48 · October 27, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🥳 A WIN FOR TRANSIT ACCESS

🌉 TONIGHT: SRT BRIDGE TOUR

🍻 MONDAY: SOUTH STREET MEETUP

🗳️ GET READY TO VOTE

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

✍️ PHILADELPHIA2050 Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission's Philadelphia2050 plan will shape the future of housing, transportation, and public spaces in our city. Take their survey here and show your support for more housing, safer streets, and better public spaces!

 

🛠️ FIX THE SOUTH STREET BRIDGE

Far too many bicyclists are getting hit by cars on the South Street Bridge--tell the city to fast-track safety improvements!

 

🚗💨 DON'T LOWER FINES FOR RECKLESS DRIVERS

Council Bill 260699 would weaken our city's lifesaving speed camera program by cutting speed camera fines, even for reckless drivers going 30+ mph over the speed limit--tell Council: Say NO to Bill 260699!

 

💰🚲 SAVE FEDERAL BIKE FUNDING

DOT Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress to end federal funding for bike lanes and even remove existing bike lanes from roads that receive federal funding. Tell your representatives in Congress: Save Our Bike Lanes!

 

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

📅 EVENTS

Oct 29

Pitchfest: Transportation

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

Transportation Initiative at Penn is hosting an event designed to connect transportation-focused public agencies with faculty and staff at the University of Pennsylvania to collaborate on applied research projects. Public agency staff are invited to give low-stakes, two-minute pitches on short-term, high-impact projects that could benefit from external expert support.
Oct 29

Transit Forward Philly Book Club: The Lost Subways of North America

5:30 to 7:00 PM · TFP Office, 1500 Walnut St, Ste 1107

Discuss Jake Berman's The Lost Subways of North America for Transit Forward Philly's October book club.
Oct 29

Car Brain Documentary Premiere

7:00 PM · Bok Auditorium, 1901 S 9th St

Attend the free world premiere of Car Brain, a feature documentary about parking and the crisis around car ownership in Philly. The film covers the PPA, the activists of Philly Bike action, and a host of eccentric Philadelphians
Nov 2

November 5th Square Meetup - Saving South Street

6:00 to 8:00 PM · Nikki Lopez, 304 South St, 2nd Floor

Join us for our November social meetup, focused on South Street! We're hosing a data-driven look at more than 50 years of South Street’s economic history and how its vacancy and corridor-health trends compare with East Passyunk, featuring special guests Eleanor Ingersoll, Executive Director of the South Street Headhouse District, and Brandon Engelhardt, author of the Saving South Street study.
Nov 3

Vote Transit - Philly

7:30 AM · Transit Forward Philly Office, 1500 Walnut St, Ste 1107

When transit riders vote, we win. Canvass Philadelphia transit riders to help them make a plan to vote in the November 3rd election.
Nov 4

DVRPC: Transit-Oriented Development

5:30 PM · DVRPC office (190 N Independence Mall W, 8th Fl) or Zoom

DVRPC’s Public Participation Task Force is hosting a hybrid meeting about how SEPTA and NJ Transit are supporting the creation of livable and walkable places near transit stations.
Nov 10

Accelerate: SEPTA’s Best-in-Class Vision for the Authority & Region

12:00 to 1:00 PM · Virtual via Zoom

Design Advocacy Group will host SEPTA GM Scott Sauer for a virtual presentation on the agency's Accelerate plan. They'll discuss plans for new trolley and subway fleets, more frequent service, and bringing high-quality transit within reach of millions more residents and jobs.
Nov 15

World Day of Remembrance

11:00 AM · Butler Triangle (between Germantown Ave, Broad St, W Butler St)

Join us to honor those who have lost their lives or been impacted by roadway crashes. We will hear from local elected officials, city staff, community leaders, and families who have lost their loved ones to traffic violence.
Nov 21

Housing Justice Film Series

1:00 to 2:30 PM · AAPA Temple, 6008 Germantown Ave

Join Germantown Residents for Economic Alternatives for a film screening and discussion, with free popcorn and beverages.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

Philadelphia Business Journal / Market East revival could make housing 'a high priority,' city official says

The Inquirer / A 68-unit apartment building is planned for the South Broad Street surface parking lot flanked by Mario Lanza mural

Pew / Accessory Dwelling Units Can Meaningfully Boost Housing Supply

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

CityNerd / (Video) How Does Philadelphia Even Exist

🚌 TRANSIT

PhillyVoice / SEPTA affordability programs would be permanent under proposed Philly law

The Inquirer / SEPTA ridership hits record high since pre-pandemic. But overall ridership still has not fully recovered.

NBC Philadelphia / SEPTA's real-time tracking tools back online after cybersecurity precaution

🚲 MOBILITY

The Inquirer / ‘Affordability’ gone wild? Proposal would reward traffic scofflaws with ticket amnesty | Shackamaxon

Pennsylvania Capital Star / Bill to legalize, regulate and restrict who can ride e-scooters passes state House

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Office of Councilmember O’Rourke / Communications Manager

Glitter / Ambassador

Reclaim Philadelphia / Executive Director

Office of State Rep. Elizabeth Fiedler / Constituent Services Advisor

Impact Services / Portfolio Manager

Clean Air Council / Trail and Watershed Outreach Coordinator

Tree House Books / Development Director

University City District

  • Senior Manager of Advancement, Workforce
  • Executive Operations Coordinator

Bread & Roses Community Fund

  • Program Associate
  • Senior Director of Development and Communications 

City of Philadelphia

  • Environmental Stewardship Specialist
  • Environmental Stewardship Manager
  • Green Stormwater Infrastructure Program Manager (Parks and Recreation)

Only One / Chief of Staff

Friends of the Wissahickon / Business Manager

Philadelphia Corporation for Aging / Quality Improvement Manager

 

Do You Like This Newsletter and Our Advocacy Work?

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents. Donations are not tax deductible.

Website Instagram Become a Member Volunteer

Far too many bicyclists are getting hit by cars on the South Street Bridge--tell the city to fast-track safety improvements!

 

🚗💨 DON'T LOWER FINES FOR RECKLESS DRIVERS

Council Bill 260699 would weaken our city's lifesaving speed camera program by cutting speed camera fines, even for reckless drivers going 30+ mph over the speed limit--tell Council: Say NO to Bill 260699!

 

💰🚲 SAVE FEDERAL BIKE FUNDING

DOT Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress to end federal funding for bike lanes and even remove existing bike lanes from roads that receive federal funding. Tell your representatives in Congress: Save Our Bike Lanes!

 

✍️ CENTER CITY CONCOURSE SURVEY

Center City District is exploring ways to reimagine the Center City Concourse--respond to their survey to share your feedback!

 

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

📅 EVENTS

Oct 13

Transit Postcard Happy Hour

6:00 to 8:00 PM · Dock Street Brewery South, 2118 Washington Ave

Write postcards in support of a Transit Access Fund for Philadelphia. Supplies provided. All ages are welcome.
Oct 13

Roosevelt Blvd Open House: Pratt St to Old Lincoln Hwy

6:00 to 8:00 PM · KleinLife, 10100 Jamison Ave

Attend for an open house plans display for the Roosevelt Boulevard - TOMORROW - Section RB2 (Pratt Street to Old Lincoln Highway).
Oct 14

Transit Access Fund Advocacy Day

9:00 AM to 12:00 PM · City Hall

Help make the Transit Access Fund happen with a day of advocacy inside City Hall. Bring ID for City Hall security.
Oct 14

Roosevelt Blvd Open House: Broad St to Pratt St

6:00 to 8:00 PM · Esperanza Arts Center, 4261 N 5th St

Attend for an open house plans display for the Roosevelt Boulevard - TOMORROW - Section RB1 (Broad Street to Pratt Street).
Oct 14

The Original Transit-Oriented City: Transit-Oriented Communities and Philadelphia’s Next Era

5:30 to 7:00 PM · Village of Industry & Art, 320 S Broad St

Join Design Advocacy Group and representatives from DVRPC, SEPTA, and the Philadelphia City Planning Commission for a discussion on how to leverage the region’s transit network to create and sustain neighborhoods that prioritize people and make walking, biking, and transit convenient, attractive transportation choices.
Oct 15

Philadelphia Trail Plan Open House

5:00 to 7:30 PM · LOVE Park Saucer, 1500 JFK Blvd

Help shape the future of trails in our city. Attend the open house to learn more about the trail plan, share your ideas, and help create better trail connections.
Oct 17

Making All Stops - Transit Arts Event

1:00 to 3:00 PM · The Rotunda, 4014 Walnut St

Making All Stops is a community storytelling production where SEPTA riders read their own short pieces about their metro memories, their SEPTA stories, their moments of transit and trust, care and connection. To be a part of it, fill out this form.
Oct 19

Vote Transit - Montgomery County

6:45 AM · North Wales Station

When transit riders vote, we win. Canvass North Wales Station to help transit riders make a plan to vote in the November 3rd election. We'll share resources for voter registration, requesting a mail ballot, and finding your polling location on election day.
Oct 22

Give Public Comment in Support of the Transit Access Fund

9:30 AM to 1:00 PM · City Hall

Give public comment and let City Council know why we need the Transit Access Fund. Don't forget your ID for City Hall security.
Oct 24

Housing Justice Film Series: Housing Issues in Philadelphia

1:00 to 2:30 PM · AAPA Temple, 6008 Germantown Ave

Join Germantown Residents for Economic Alternatives for a film screening and discussion, with free popcorn and beverages.
Oct 26

Vote Transit - Bucks County

7:00 AM · Cornwells Heights Station

When transit riders vote, we win. Canvass Cornwells Heights Station to help transit riders make a plan to vote in the November 3rd election. We'll share resources for voter registration, requesting a mail ballot, and finding your polling location on election day.
Oct 29

Pitchfest: Transportation

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

Transportation Initiative at Penn is hosting an event designed to connect transportation-focused public agencies with faculty and staff at the University of Pennsylvania to collaborate on applied research projects. Public agency staff are invited to give low-stakes, two-minute pitches on short-term, high-impact projects that could benefit from external expert support.
Oct 29

Car Brain Documentary Premiere

7:00 PM · Bok Auditorium, 1901 S 9th St

Attend the free world premiere of Car Brain, a feature documentary about parking and the crisis around car ownership in Philly. The film covers the PPA, the activists of Philly Bike action, and a host of eccentric Philadelphians
Nov 2

November 5th Square Meetup - Saving South Street

6:00 to 8:00 PM · Nikki Lopez, 304 South St, 2nd Floor

Join us for our November social meetup, focused on South Street! We're hosing a data-driven look at more than 50 years of South Street’s economic history and how its vacancy and corridor-health trends compare with East Passyunk, featuring special guests Eleanor Ingersoll, Executive Director of the South Street Headhouse District, and Brandon Engelhardt, author of the Saving South Street study.
Nov 3

Vote Transit - Philly

7:30 AM · Transit Forward Philly Office, 1500 Walnut St, Ste 1107

When transit riders vote, we win. Canvass Philadelphia transit riders to help them make a plan to vote in the November 3rd election.
Nov 15

World Day of Remembrance

11:00 AM · Butler Triangle (between Germantown Ave, Broad St, W Butler St)

Join us to honor those who have lost their lives or been impacted by roadway crashes. We will hear from local elected officials, city staff, community leaders, and families who have lost their loved ones to traffic violence.
Nov 21

Housing Justice Film Series

1:00 to 2:30 PM · AAPA Temple, 6008 Germantown Ave

Join Germantown Residents for Economic Alternatives for a film screening and discussion, with free popcorn and beverages.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

The Inquirer / Washington Square West Historic District overturned by a judge for a second time

The Philadelphia Citizen / No Preservation Tax on Washington Square West

The Inquirer / SEPTA wants to transform a historic East Passyunk trolley substation into something new

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Axios / New streetery designs could boost Philadelphia's outdoor dining scene

🚌 TRANSIT

The Inquirer / Accelerate to the modern SEPTA the region deserves

Audacy / Philly students, school officials debate extending student SEPTA pass hours in City Council hearing

TribLIVE / Amtrak announces date for 2nd route from Pittsburgh to New York

🚲 MOBILITY

Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia / We Can Make Philadelphia’s Streets Safer Without Building A Surveillance Network

WHYY / New Jersey’s e-bike law was changed to improve safety. It’s being criticized by riders, bicycle shops and advocacy groups

6ABC / Parent hit by car during National Walk and Roll to School Day in South Philadelphia

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Clean Air Council / Trail and Watershed Outreach Coordinator

Mission First Housing Group / Real Estate Development Manager (Philly & DC)

Tree House Books / Development Director

University City District

  • Senior Manager of Advancement, Workforce
  • Executive Operations Coordinator

Histories Collaborative of Philadelphia / Executive Director / Chief Collaborative Officer

Public Interest Law Center / Paralegal

Bread & Roses Community Fund

  • Program Associate
  • Senior Director of Development and Communications 

City of Philadelphia

  • Environmental Stewardship Specialist
  • Environmental Stewardship Manager
  • Green Stormwater Infrastructure Program Manager (Parks and Recreation)
  • Chief of Staff - Managing Director's Office

RiSE / Real Estate Accelerator

Philadelphia Housing Authority / Construction Cost Estimator

Only One / Chief of Staff

Friends of the Wissahickon / Business Manager

Philadelphia Corporation for Aging / Quality Improvement Manager

 

Do You Like This Newsletter and Our Advocacy Work?

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents. Donations are not tax deductible.

Website Instagram Become a Member Volunteer

info@5thsqadvocacy.org · 700 S. 7th St Unit 6780, Philadelphia PA 19147
